intro.heading: Roofing Built for Spring
intro.body_p1: Spring developed rapidly during the 1980s and 1990s as one of the Greater Houston area's most active suburban expansion zones. That housing stock is now entering a critical age window — original roofs in many Spring neighborhoods are at or past their typical service life for asphalt shingles in the Texas climate. Compounding the age factor is Spring's high annual rainfall — proximity to Spring Creek means roofs here are routinely exposed to the moisture and drainage stress that accelerates wear on shingles, flashing, and gutters alike.
intro.body_p2: Home Team works throughout the Spring area to help homeowners understand the actual condition of their roof. We conduct free, thorough inspections that cover shingles, flashing, gutters, decking, and attic ventilation, then walk you through exactly what we found using photos and plain language. Whether your home needs targeted repair after a hail event or a full replacement, we deliver honest recommendations based on what we see.

items.q: Spring has a lot of 1980s and 1990s homes — when should those roofs be replaced?
items.a: Standard three-tab and early architectural shingles installed during Spring's main development era are now 30–40 years old in many neighborhoods — well past the typical 20–25 year lifespan for asphalt shingles in the Texas heat and humidity. If your Spring home has never had a roof replacement, an inspection is the right starting point. A professional can document the current condition, identify any hidden damage from past storms, and give you a clear picture of how much useful life remains. Waiting until there is an active leak typically means more damage to decking, insulation, and interior finishes.

items.q: Are impact-resistant shingles worth it for a Spring home?
items.a: Class 4 impact-resistant shingles — the highest rating under the UL 2218 standard — are significantly more resistant to hail damage than standard asphalt shingles. For Spring homeowners who have dealt with repeated hail events, upgrading at replacement time reduces the likelihood of storm damage in future years. Some Texas insurance carriers may offer premium discounts for Class 4 installations — coverage and discount decisions are made by your insurance provider. Home Team can walk through whether impact-resistant materials make sense for your specific project and what the cost difference looks like compared to standard architectural shingles.

items.q: What are the signs that my Spring home's roof has hail damage?
items.a: Hail damage on asphalt shingles often appears as dark spots or bruising where the granule layer has been knocked away, exposing the underlying fiberglass mat. From the ground, look for dented gutters, damaged downspout fins, and granule accumulation in drainage areas. Damaged window screens are another common indicator. Hail impact that is invisible from the ground can still fracture the shingle's structural layer and significantly shorten the roof's remaining lifespan. A professional inspection after any notable hailstorm is the most reliable way to assess actual damage.

items.q: How does Spring's rainfall affect my roof compared to drier parts of Texas?
items.a: The Greater Houston area — including Spring — averages significantly more annual rainfall than cities like Dallas or Austin, and Spring Creek and the surrounding drainage network can make localized flooding more likely. For roofing, persistent rainfall puts ongoing stress on flashing seals, penetration points around chimneys and vents, and any areas where water has a chance to pool. Gutters and downspouts that are undersized or improperly sloped can cause water to back up against the fascia and underlayment. Home Team evaluates drainage and runoff management as part of every inspection in the Spring area.

topic1.heading: Intense Heat and UV Exposure
topic1.body: Houston-area summers push roof surface temperatures well above the ambient air temperature. Over time, heat and UV radiation break down shingle granules, accelerate asphalt oxidation, and shorten the functional life of an improperly ventilated roof. Quality attic ventilation is not optional in this climate — it is a performance requirement.

topic2.heading: Hail and Severe Storm Seasons
topic2.body: The greater Houston area — including Spring — experiences frequent severe weather with hail that can cause damage invisible from the ground. Bruised shingles, granule loss, and cracked underlayment require close professional inspection. Even minor impact can allow moisture intrusion that worsens significantly over time in the area's humid climate.

topic3.heading: Rainfall and Drainage
topic3.body: Spring sits in a high-rainfall corridor, and proximity to Spring Creek and its drainage network means heavy rain events are frequent. Persistent moisture tests every flashing seal and penetration on a roof. Gutters that cannot handle peak rainfall rates allow water to back up against the fascia — a common issue on the 1980s and 1990s homes that define many Spring neighborhoods.

topic4.heading: Shingle Selection for the Texas Climate
topic4.body: Not all asphalt shingles perform equally in the Houston-area climate. Architectural shingles with Class 4 impact resistance ratings offer significantly better durability against hail than standard three-tab designs. Algae-resistant shingles — which use copper-infused granules to inhibit growth — address the persistent algae streaking common on roofs in high-humidity environments like Spring. When replacing an aging roof, material selection is an opportunity to improve performance, not just restore it.
